chunks: Al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: “A human being has thirty-one openings, and in each opening there are three camels and one-fifth of a camel.”
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report accords with the doctrine of some of the generality, and we do not act upon it. Practice is according to the reports that we have presented earlier.

key_terms.أَبْعِرَةٍ: camels, used here as the unit of diyyah valuation
key_terms.الْأَخْبَارِ: the transmitted reports upon which legal practice is based
key_terms.الْخَبَرُ: the report or hadith under discussion
key_terms.الْعَامَّةِ: the generality, referring here to non-Imami authorities
key_terms.بَعِيرٍ: a camel, the standard compensation unit in diyyah calculations
key_terms.ثَغْرَةً: a bodily opening or orifice in the legal context of injury compensation
key_terms.مُوَافِقٌ: in agreement or conformity with a particular doctrinal position

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith in Tahdhib al-Ahkam say about the diyyah of bodily openings, and is it acted upon in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith concerns a legal assessment related to bodily injuries and assigns a quantified diyyah value to bodily openings. Shaykh al-Tusi then states that this report agrees with the view of some non-Imami authorities and that it is not acted upon, with practice instead based on the earlier reports he cited.
